angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 688,743 km at 112.83 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.8626 +/- 0.0181 mas (same row, RUWE 1.17): 112.83 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.99 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-426 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract): 688,743 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-426 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5750 +/- 62 K from Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-426 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-426 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-426.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.447, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
